bullets.title: FOMC hold expected today; Warsh press conference seen as short-lived catalyst
bullets.body: Fed Chair Warsh is widely expected to hold rates unchanged, with BofA the lone outlier calling for a hike (low conviction). Analysts note Warsh speaks more for himself than the committee — a break from Powell/Yellen/Bernanke norms — meaning subsequent Fedspeak from voting members will carry more lasting market impact. 62% of investors expect mixed/negligible market reaction to the press conference, the highest such reading since Q1.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler AI capex at ~$770B (100% of OCF); debt financing surged from 9% to 32% of capex
bullets.body: AI-related issuers are now trading 115bps over Treasuries vs. 78bps for broader IG, with debt financing of capex rising from 9% in FY24 to 32% over the last 12 months. Goldman expects hyperscaler debt issuance to rise 60% to ~$420B next year. MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN earnings after close today are the key event for validating the AI capex-to-revenue conversion narrative.

bullets.title: GOOGL Cloud expected to crush (+100-115% Y/Y) on TPU sales; Search may miss ~100bps
bullets.body: JPM estimates implied GOOGL TPU sales of $5-7B in Q3, with 2027 Cloud growth expected above +100% Y/Y. A negative 3P check points to a Search revenue miss of ~100bps, creating a mixed setup into tonight's print. OpenAI is buying Google TPUs to diversify away from Nvidia, a structural positive for GOOGL Cloud margin expansion.

bullets.title: MSFT Azure expected to re-accelerate to ~47% Y/Y; FY27 capex modeled at $213-237B
bullets.body: Consensus expects Azure growth of ~44-47% Y/Y in FQ1 as Copilot workloads grow 4x YTD. UBS sees a 2pt beat to ~47% with FQ2 guidance of 46-47%. FY27 capex estimates range from $213B (UBS) to $237B (Citi), representing ~60-63% Y/Y growth — the cost-of-capital scrutiny around this figure is the primary market debate.

bullets.title: SK Hynix blowout: memory sold out through 2029, expects shortage through 2030
bullets.body: SK Hynix reported Q3 OPM of 79.7% with revenue +328% Y/Y; DRAM and HBM capacity is effectively sold out through 2029, with LTAs covering >50% of 2027-2028 production across 14 major CSP customers. The company announced a ₩100tn (~$75.5B) shareholder return program. US memory names (MU +3.5%, SNDK +4.1%) rallied in sympathy, with the KOSPI +7% overnight.

bullets.title: AI financing overhangs cleared: META $97.5B raise, SpaceX $40B GPU deal, AVGO $63B SPV
bullets.body: A cluster of mega-financing announcements — META's ~$100B capital raise, SpaceX's $40B GPU deal, and Broadcom's $63B custom-chip SPV — sparked back-to-back 1%+ Nasdaq gains Monday-Tuesday, the first time in ~3 months. Goldman noted hedge fund net tech exposure was near yearly lows heading in; the two largest institutional tech liquidations on record preceded this bounce. Anthropic's S-1 filing keeps a November IPO on track with $650B+ in compute commitments disclosed.

bullets.title: S&P futures +0.2% at 7773; 10-year yield at 5.00%; WTI +1.7% to $101.56 on Iran tensions
bullets.body: Pre-market setup is modestly constructive with SPX futures up 0.2%, though the 10-year yield holding at 5.00% is a headwind for valuation. Oil is rallying on WSJ reports of a planned U.S. military campaign against Iran post-midterms, with Brent cited at $115-119 in some frameworks. Energy and tanker stocks are up 2-5% in sympathy.

bullets.title: 3Q26 earnings beat rate solid: 78% topping estimates, EPS tracking +30.9% growth
bullets.body: UBS reports 78% of S&P 500 companies have beaten estimates with aggregate EPS beats of 5.7%; the index is on pace for 30.9% EPS growth in 3Q26 vs. the 28.7% initial expectation. Notably, EPS misses are being punished less than usual — misses outperforming the S&P by 0.7 points vs. the typical 2-point underperformance — suggesting the market is in a forgiving mood for near-term guidance shortfalls.

bullets.title: VRT +16.5% pre-market as AI power infrastructure demand drives massive beat-and-raise
bullets.body: Vertiv reported Q3 revenue of $4.31B vs. FactSet $3.75B, raising FY guidance to $14.45-14.85B. Americas organic growth accelerated to 66% with 100% order growth. The print is being read as a strong confirmation of the AI data center build cycle, with MOD +7% and FPS +6.5% in sympathy.

bullets.title: Corporate buyback windows nearly doubling to 50% by end of week — technical support for equities
bullets.body: Buyback blackout windows are expected to lift sharply, with the share of S&P 500 companies in open windows nearly doubling from ~27% to ~50% by end of this week. This is a mechanical source of equity demand into November and a near-term technical positive for the tape.

bullets.title: Consumer confidence rebounded to 91.7 in October but forward expectations remain recessionary
bullets.body: The Conference Board consumer confidence index hit 91.7, its highest since June, but forward expectations remain at 72.6 — below the 80-level threshold historically associated with recession risk. PSC Macro separately flags low-end consumer income accelerating faster than middle/high-income cohorts, with non-discretionary CPI below 2% Y/Y supporting purchasing power.

bullets.title: AI capex growth slowing: ~100% in 2026, expected to decelerate to 30% in 2027, 22% in 2028
bullets.body: Jefferies and Semis Daily both flag that AI earnings growth is expected to slow materially from the ~100% pace of 2026 to roughly 30% in 2027 and 22% in 2028. Financing constraints are viewed as a 2028+ risk — 2026-2027 DC deployments (~27GW planned for 2027) appear funded, but 1H27 land-clearing decisions are critical for 2028 capacity-on-date outcomes. Elon Musk flagged 200+ neocloud companies at collapse risk.

bullets.title: Global smartphone shipments forecast -15% YoY in 2026-2027; Chinese vendors down 23%
bullets.body: Elevated memory costs are pressuring affordability and OEM margins, driving a projected 15% decline in global smartphone shipments in both 2026 and 2027, with Chinese vendors expected down 23% in 2027. A recovery is unlikely before 2028. This creates a direct headwind for AAPL's iPhone 18 cycle — FY27 EPS is estimated 13% below current consensus.

bullets.title: ENPH -19% on deeply missed guidance; baseline demand now ~$200M/quarter
bullets.body: Enphase guided 4Q26 revenue of $225-255M, well below consensus of $257-299M, with ongoing gross margin pressure from tariffs and battery storage mix. Opco downgraded to Perform; Mizuho cut 2027 revenue estimates by 14% to ~$1B ($800M residential + $200M growth vectors). SEDG fell 8.6% in sympathy. Higher rates and disappointing US solar installation activity are the primary demand headwinds.

bullets.title: Hedgeye bearish on AI semis: KOSPI -34% from peak, SOXL retail chase seen as bubble signal
bullets.body: Hedgeye flags the South Korean bear market as down 34% from its June cycle peak despite the SK Hynix bounce, characterizing the $5.5B MOC buy order in SOXL (3x levered semis ETF) as retail chasing in a thinning liquidity environment. Their macro framework has Brent at $115-119 in bullish TRADE/TREND, with the long oil/short semis thesis intact. They are short NVDA, AMZN, META, GOOGL, and NFLX on their risk-range signals.

bullets.title: Fed press conference dynamics: dovish Warsh = risk-off, hawkish = risk-on (inverted reaction)
bullets.body: Multiple analysts flag an unusual inversion in today's FOMC reaction function: if Warsh downplays AI credit risks and financial conditions tightening, the market may read that as complacency (risk-off); if he sounds hawkish on financial conditions remaining accommodative, markets may rally on relief that the Fed has room. December 25bp hike remains on the table, conditional on CPI acceleration and oil prices.

bullets.title: Russell 2000 outperforming YTD (+13.6% vs S&P +12.8%) but technicals show vulnerability
bullets.body: The Russell 2000 was up 1.2% on Oct 27, outperforming the S&P by 0.6%, with 3Q26 small-cap earnings aggregating +7.7% above expectations. However, Hedgeye flags IWM/RUT at -3.9% downside within its trade range and -8.1% from cycle peak, with small-cap EPS growth decelerating into a Quad2-to-Quad4 shift in 1H27.

bullets.title: Oil at $101.56 WTI (+1.7%) on Iran military campaign reports; macro regime shifting to Quad2
bullets.body: WTI is up 1.7% to $101.56 with Brent cited at $115-119 in more aggressive macro frameworks, driven by WSJ reporting on planned U.S. military action against Iran post-midterms. The oil rally is feeding into Hedgeye's Quad2 growth/inflation framework, which they argue the Fed will be forced to acknowledge on upcoming CPI prints. The RBA governor separately warned of upside inflation risks from the oil-and-AI boom.

bullets.title: Ackman bullish on AMZN/META/MSFT; bought AMZN during tariff selloff
bullets.body: Bill Ackman's Pershing Square has roughly one-third of its portfolio in AMZN, META, and MSFT. He bought AMZN shares during Trump tariff-related volatility and added META/MSFT after AI capex-driven selloffs. Ackman views market volatility from passive ownership and leveraged short-term trading as creating entry points in quality businesses, and sees AI as an accelerant of global growth via low-cost intelligence.

bullets.title: Visa beats on volumes; FY27 VAS guidance (low-to-mid-20s%) below recent +30%+ run rate
bullets.body: Visa Q4 EPS $3.48 beat consensus $3.44 with gross revenue growth of 15% and global payment volumes up ~10%. Value Added Services grew 31% in FQ4 but FY27 VAS guidance stepped down to low-to-mid-twenties, below recent performance, due to elevated client renewals (~25% of volume base renewing vs. normal 15-20%). Street PTs range $440-479; Citi maintains Buy at $440.
